content.user_title: Analyze Stocks with Graham and Buffett Frameworks
content.value_statement: Value investors need consistent checks across valuation, quality, and financial statements. This skill applies Graham and Buffett frameworks with reconciliation, rankings, warnings, and source citations.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes one stock using Graham six-factor scoring and dynamic value-trap adjustments.
Screens up to 300 symbols for NCAV, valuation, dividends, debt coverage, and earnings stability.
Evaluates one company across moat, financial health, management, valuation, and long-term visibility.
Ranks three to five Buffett-style candidates after quantitative and qualitative filters.
Reconciles financial statements, shares, and market capitalization before scoring.
Produces source appendices with endpoints, periods, timestamps, and labeled web sources.
limitations: Requires Longbridge CLI or MCP for primary data. Web search covers only genuine data gaps.
Does not provide personalized investment advice or account for individual risk tolerance.
Graham NCAV excludes financial institutions, REITs, negative-equity firms, and holding shells.
Results depend on source completeness, reporting periods, and framework assumptions.

use_cases.title: Deep-Value Review
use_cases.description: Assess one stock using NCAV, valuation ratios, earnings stability, value-trap signals, and a margin-of-safety price range.

use_cases.title: Research Watchlist Screening
use_cases.description: Rank an index or watchlist by Graham criteria while documenting exclusions, data anomalies, waiting costs, and source coverage.

use_cases.title: Quality Compounder Discovery
use_cases.description: Find companies with durable moats, strong returns, positive cash flow, disciplined capital allocation, and reasonable valuations.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Quality Stock
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze AAPL.US with the Buffett moat framework. Explain each dimension, valuation, minimum holding period, data limitations, and sources in clear English.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Graham Diagnostic
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate 00700.HK with the Graham framework. Show NCAV, six-factor scoring, value-trap checks, safety-margin prices, holding-period range, and the source appendix.

prompt_templates.title: Screen a Major Index
prompt_templates.prompt: Screen the S&P 500 for Graham-style deep-value candidates. Return the top 10, explain exclusions and warnings, and list all data sources.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Custom Quality Filters
prompt_templates.prompt: Screen my watchlist [SYMBOLS] for Buffett-style quality compounders. Require five-year average ROE above [X]%, positive three-year FCF, and PE below [Y]. Reconcile statements, rank three to five candidates, and explain threshold overrides.

output_examples.input: Analyze Example Corp with the Buffett moat framework.
output_examples.output: Example Corp receives a four-star quality rating. The report explains moat evidence, financial trends, valuation, holding period, limitations, and cited sources.

output_examples.input: Screen my 50-stock watchlist for Graham candidates.
output_examples.output: The result ranks qualifying stocks by adjusted score and NCAV ratio. It also lists exclusions, value-trap warnings, waiting costs, and data sources.

output_examples.input: Evaluate a stock whose statements do not reconcile.
output_examples.output: No score is issued. The report names the failed reconciliation check, explains the discrepancy, and identifies the affected source data.

best_practices: Provide an exact ticker, market, and preferred framework.
State the screening universe, investment horizon, and any threshold changes.
Review source dates, reconciliation notes, exclusions, and data limitations before using results.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a high score as a buy or sell recommendation.
Do not apply NCAV analysis to banks, insurers, REITs, or other excluded financial businesses.
Do not compare results built from mismatched periods or incomplete financial statements.

faq.question: Does this skill provide investment advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides framework-based research for informational use and does not consider personal finances or risk tolerance.

faq.question: Which markets can it analyze?
faq.answer: It supports United States, Hong Kong, and A-share symbols when the required Longbridge data is available.

faq.question: What data sources does it use?
faq.answer: It uses Longbridge CLI first, MCP as fallback, and labeled web sources only for genuine data gaps.

faq.question: What happens when financial statements do not reconcile?
faq.answer: The skill halts scoring or removes the affected row. It reports the failed check and discrepancy.

faq.question: Can I change the screening thresholds?
faq.answer: Yes. You can override supported thresholds and ranking rules. The output records each change.

faq.question: How many stocks can one screen cover?
faq.answer: The documented default ceiling is 300 symbols. Buffett screens return three to five candidates, while Graham screens can return a larger ranking.
